senses.definition: (obsolete) Mean; dirty; contemptible; scrubby.

quotes.text: How solitary, how scrub, does this town look!
quotes.reference: 1743, Horace Walpole, letter to Sir Horace Mann:

quotes.text: No little scrub joint shall come on my board.
quotes.reference: 1729, Jonathan Swift, The Grand Question Debated of Hamilton's Bawn:

senses.definition: (uncountable) A thicket or jungle, often specified by the name of the prevailing plant.

quotes.text: I stumbled along through the young pines and huckleberry bushes. Pretty soon I struck into a sort of path that, I cal'lated, might lead to the road I was hunting for. It twisted and turned, and, the first thing I knew, made a sudden bend around a bunch of bayberry scrub and opened out into a big clear space like a lawn.
quotes.reference: 1913, Joseph C[rosby] Lincoln, chapter I, in Mr. Pratt’s Patients, New York, N.Y.; London: D[aniel] Appleton and Company, →OCLC:

senses.definition: (uncountable) Vegetation judged to be of inferior quality or of little use to humans, though sometimes thick and impenetrable, growing in poor soil or in sand; also, brush.

(countable, US, stock breeding) One of the common livestock of a region of no particular breed or not of pure breed, especially when inferior in size, etc.; particularly a male animal poorly suited for breeding.
(countable, derogatory) One who labors hard and lives meanly.

quotes.text: A sorry scrub, said Mr. High-mind.
We should go there in as proper a manner possible; nor altogether like the scrubs about us.
quotes.reference: 1766, Oliver Goldsmith, The Vicar of Wakefield:

quotes.text: I daresay we can find one of those devoted, hard-working little scrubs who are glad to come for nothing and live on the table leavings.
quotes.reference: 1934, Ernest Bramah, The Bravo of London:

senses.definition: (countable, slang, derogatory) One who is incompetent or unable to complete easy tasks.
examples: Wow, she really scored 0? What a scrub!

A scrub is a guy that thinks he's fly
And is also known as a buster
Always talkin' about what he wants
And just sits on his broke ass […]

quotes.text:
You triflin', good-for-nothin' type of brother
Silly me, why haven't I found another?
A baller, when times get hard I need someone to help me out
Instead of a scrub like you who don't know what a man's about
quotes.reference: 1999 May 31, Beyoncé Knowles, Kelly Rowland, LeToya Luckett, Kevin Briggs, Kandi Burruss, “Bills, Bills, Bills”, in The Writing's on the Wall, performed by Destiny's Child, track 3:

senses.definition: (countable, sports, slang) One not on the first team of players; a substitute.
(countable, online gaming, slang, derogatory) A player who whines when outmatched by other players, sometimes by blaming the game mechanics or even accusing the other players of cheating.
(transitive) To rub hard; to wash with rubbing; usually, to rub with a wet brush, or with something coarse or rough, for the purpose of cleaning or brightening
(intransitive) To rub anything hard, especially with a wet brush; to scour
(intransitive, figuratively) To be diligent and penurious
examples: to scrub hard for a living

senses.definition: (transitive) To call off a scheduled event; to cancel.
examples: Engineers had to scrub the satellite launch due to bad weather.

senses.definition: (databases, transitive) To eliminate or to correct data from a set of records to bring it inline with other similar datasets
examples: The street segment data from the National Post Office will need to be scrubbed before it can be integrated into our system.

senses.definition: (media) To move a recording tape back and forth with a scrubbing motion to produce a scratching sound, or to do so by a similar use of a control on an editing system.
(media) To maneuver the play position on a media editing system by using a scroll bar or touch-based interface.
An instance of scrubbing.
A cancellation.

quotes.text: Unacceptable winds aloft caused four scrubs and one hold; adverse weather caused a scrub; […]

senses.definition: A worn-out brush.

quotes.text: A scrub [broom worn out] Scopa detrita.
quotes.reference: 1752, Robert Ainsworth, Thesaurus Linguae Latinae Compendiarius:

senses.definition: One who scrubs.
That which scrubs.
(medicine, in the plural) Clothing worn while performing surgery.
(by extension, in the plural) Any medical uniform consisting of a short-sleeved shirt and pants (trousers).

quotes.text: A man dressed as a lab tech, his blue scrubs startlingly pale against the vivid red and black chaos, moved into sight from behind the SUV. He carried an assault rifle.

senses.definition: (slang, obsolete) Informal attire or dress code; morning dress

quotes.text: The third, which was as homely as its name, and which she reserved for scouring the country and such like rough usage in quite private rural life, was her "Scrub."
quotes.reference: 1876, “Hightum, Titum, and Scrub!”, in The Leisure Hour:

quotes.text: For one of Lucia's quaint ideas was to divide dresses into three classes, "Hightum," "Tightum" and "Scrub."
